title: Trains to Blackpool
from: stations across the North West, Yorkshire, London and Glasgow
lead: These are the trains I would look at for the Blackpool Air Show. Blackpool North is the station to aim for, about 15 minutes on foot from the Tower and the middle of the display. Northern runs straight into Blackpool North from Manchester, Manchester Airport, Liverpool, Preston, Leeds and York, and if you’re coming from London Euston, Lancaster or Glasgow you change at Preston, where there are about four trains an hour on to Blackpool. From London Kings Cross you change at York instead. Pick your station, a day and a time below and the map shows every station on the way.
facts: About four trains an hour from Preston
ysIntro: This is the station I would get off at for the Blackpool Air Show. The details below follow the train you pick further down the page.
walkLine: I would walk down Talbot Road to Talbot Square and North Pier, then south along the promenade to the Tower. Allow 15 minutes, or a bit more in the crowds.
walkBack: Head back up Talbot Road from Talbot Square to the station, about 15 minutes. After the last display the station fills quickly, so allow a bit longer.
tip: After the last display the station fills quickly. I would get something to eat in town and catch a later train, or leave before the final act if you have a connection to make.
Trains into Blackpool get really busy on show days, so I would buy your ticket in advance, allow extra time and check for engineering work, which is common at weekends.
offTag: Get off here for the Tower
note: Due to how complicated the rail network is, this page only shows journeys from twelve main stations to Blackpool North, with the changes that work well. Times are from the National Rail timetable for Saturday 7 and Sunday 8 November 2026, checked on 2 November 2026. These are this winter’s weekend times, and the summer 2027 times will follow, so please check before you travel. Birmingham is left out for now, as that Sunday’s trains needed three changes. The line is drawn along the railway, so treat it as a guide. Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors.
gaOnly: Northern, plus the trains that connect at Preston. Northern runs most of the trains here, and I’ve added Avanti West Coast, TransPennine Express and the Scottish trains where they get you to Preston for a quick change. From Kings Cross I’ve added LNER to York, where the Blackpool train starts. I’ve only included journeys where the whole trip works on a weekend. If you’re coming from somewhere else, I would plan your trip to one of these stations first and pick it up from there.

The Air Show Village on the Tower Festival Headland opens in the morning, so if you want a front row spot on the promenade, head there first and save your pitch, then take a look round the stalls and check the food options. Visit the toilet before the flying display starts.
checks: Ear defenders packed for the children

pay: An Advance ticket is often the cheapest way to go, but it ties you to one train. With the crowds after the flying, I would think about a flexible ticket for the way home.
Think about an off peak ticket
An off peak ticket lets you choose the train on the day, which suits a big free show when you don’t know when you’ll want to go home. Check the time rules on the ticket before you buy.

A Family and Friends Railcard takes a third off adult fares and 60% off children’s fares, and it can pay for itself in one trip. Two Together, Senior, 16 to 25, 26 to 30 and Disabled Persons railcards all give a third off.
faq: Blackpool North, for most people. It’s about 15 minutes on foot to the Tower. Blackpool South and Blackpool Pleasure Beach are handy if you’re staying at the south end, but both are a long way from the display.
Is there a direct train from London?

Avanti West Coast runs one direct train a day from London Euston on weekdays and Sundays, taking about 3 hours, and none on Saturdays. Otherwise change at Preston, where there are about four trains an hour on to Blackpool North.
Yes, but not past the display. In 2026 the trams ran in two sections, Starr Gate to Manchester Square and North Pier to Fleetwood, and none stopped at the Tower or Central Pier.
Yes. Blackpool North has step free access to the platforms.
What if my train is late or cancelled?

Take a look at the live board above or the National Rail app before you leave the house. On a flexible ticket you can usually take the next train. With an Advance ticket, speak to the staff at the station.
access: Trains can work really well for Blackpool, as long as you plan the step free parts before you leave.
Book Passenger Assist on the National Rail app or by phone, and staff will meet you at the train.
Blackpool North has step free access to the platforms, and the walk to the Tower is flat.

about.Preston|Blackpool North: Out across the flat Fylde through Kirkham and Poulton, with the Tower showing on the skyline as you get close.
about.Kirkham & Wesham|Blackpool North: Through Poulton-le-Fylde and Layton, with Blackpool Tower coming into view on the way in.
about.Manchester Piccadilly|Preston: Through Bolton and Chorley and along the edge of the West Pennine Moors.
about.Manchester Airport|Preston: Up through south Manchester and the city centre, then on through Bolton and Chorley.
about.Liverpool Lime Street|Preston: Out through the cutting at Edge Hill, across St Helens to Wigan, then north up the West Coast Main Line.
about.Leeds|Preston: Along the Calder Valley through Halifax and Hebden Bridge, then over the hills by Burnley and Blackburn.
about.York|Leeds: West out of York across the Vale of York into Leeds.
about.London Euston|Preston: Up the West Coast Main Line through the Midlands and Cheshire.
about.Lancaster|Preston: South along the West Coast Main Line, across the River Wyre and past Garstang.
about.Glasgow Central|Preston: Down through the Southern Uplands and over Shap, one of the most scenic stretches of the West Coast Main Line.
about.Wigan North Western|Preston: North along the West Coast Main Line through Leyland.
about.London Kings Cross|York: Up the East Coast Main Line, one of the fastest stretches of railway in the country, through Peterborough and Doncaster.
